text: Copilot is essentially that magnified by many lines of code. It is multi-line autocomplete that is fundamentally powered by an AI model called CodeX, which is a derivative of another one that you might be familiar with, GPT-3.
speaker: Ryan J. Salva
context: Lenny asks Ryan to explain what GitHub Copilot is for listeners who aren't familiar with it. Ryan describes how Copilot evolved from basic autocomplete features that developers have used for decades. He explains that while traditional autocomplete only suggests simple completions like variable names, Copilot uses advanced AI to suggest entire blocks of code based on context, comments, and surrounding code patterns.
text_ko: 코파일럿(Copilot)은 본질적으로 많은 코드 줄로 확장된 기능이에요. 여러 줄을 한꺼번에 자동완성해 주는 멀티라인 자동완성(multi-line autocomplete)이고, 근본적으로는 코드엑스(CodeX)라는 AI 모델(AI model)이 구동해요. 코드엑스는 아마 들어보셨을 GPT-3(GPT-3)의 파생 모델이에요.
text_zh: Copilot 本质上就是把自动补全放大到多行代码，换句话说就是一种多行自动补全(multi-line autocomplete)。它背后由一个叫 CodeX 的 AI 模型(CodeX) 驱动，而 CodeX 又是从你可能熟悉的 GPT-3(GPT-3) 衍生出来的。
text_es: Copilot es, básicamente, lo mismo pero ampliado para manejar muchas líneas de código. Es un autocompletado multilínea (multi-line autocomplete) que se alimenta de un modelo de IA (AI) llamado CodeX, que a su vez deriva de otro con el que quizá ya estés familiarizado: GPT-3.
key_sentence: Copilot is fundamentally powered by an AI model called CodeX.
original_text: Copilot is essentially that magnified by many lines of code. It is multi-line autocomplete that is fundamentally powered by an AI model called CodeX, which is a derivative of another one that you might be familiar with, GPT-3. When you are in the editor, it could be VS Code, it could be IntelliJ, it could be them, essentially, as you are typing, Copilot will provide suggestions usually in kind of this italicized gray text that is really, to your point, kind of magical what it's able to infer.

vocabulary.definition: In a basic and essential way; at the core or root of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'fundamentally' is often used to emphasize the underlying principles or assumptions that drive a strategy or decision.
vocabulary.nuance: This term conveys a sense of depth and importance, suggesting that the point being made is not merely superficial.

vocabulary.definition: Something that is based on another source; not original but derived from something else.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, 'derivative' often refers to products or technologies that build upon or adapt existing innovations, highlighting their relationship to prior developments.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'derivative' can imply a lack of originality, it can also suggest a valuable evolution of existing ideas.

vocabulary.definition: A feature that predicts and suggests completions for text input based on prior data or patterns.
vocabulary.businessContext: In software development and user interface design, 'autocomplete' enhances user experience by increasing efficiency and reducing errors during data entry.
vocabulary.nuance: This term is often associated with technology products that aim to streamline user interactions, making it a positive feature in most contexts.

text: That's just labor. It's not creating. It's just typing.
speaker: Ryan J. Salva
context: Ryan continues explaining the value proposition of Copilot by describing common frustrations developers face. He argues that much of a developer's time is spent on mundane tasks like remembering API syntax or creating test data, rather than the creative problem-solving aspects of programming. Ryan positions Copilot as a tool that eliminates this 'busy work' so developers can focus on the creative and strategic aspects of coding.
text_ko: 그건 그냥 단순 노동이에요. 창조하는 일이 아니고요. 그냥 타이핑만 하는 거예요.
text_zh: 那只是体力活，不是创造性工作，就是在敲键盘而已。
text_es: Eso es trabajo rutinario, no es creación. Es solo teclear.
key_sentence: That's just labor, not creating, just typing.
original_text: The labor of remembering what's the order of parameters that need to come into a particular API, or hey, what's the particular syntax of this thing I'm supposed to do, or oh, I've got to create a bunch of dummy data that is days of the week or months in the year. That's just labor. It's not creating. It's just typing.

vocabulary.definition: Labor refers to the physical or mental effort exerted in the production of goods or services, often associated with work performed by employees.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, labor is a critical factor of production, and understanding labor costs and productivity is essential for financial planning and operational efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a sense of hard work or effort, and it is often used in discussions about workforce management, labor laws, and economic conditions.

text: We had actually created a snapshot of GitHub's public code for what we call the Arctic Code Vault, right? Essentially, this is up in like way in the Northlands of Finland, there's a seed vault. We were like, you know what?
speaker: Ryan J. Salva
context: Ryan tells the origin story of how Copilot began when OpenAI was aggressively downloading GitHub's repositories for training data. He explains that GitHub had previously created the Arctic Code Vault - a physical preservation project storing code on silver film in Finland, similar to seed vaults that preserve plant genetics. This existing dataset became the foundation for training the AI model that would become Copilot.
text_ko: 사실 저희는 GitHub 공개 코드 전체를 스냅샷(snapshot)으로 만들어 ‘아틱 코드 볼트(Arctic Code Vault)’에 보관해뒀어요. 요컨대, 이건 핀란드 북부에 있는 종자 저장고(seed vault) 같은 곳이에요. 그래서 우리는 “그래, 해보자”라고 했어요.
text_zh: 其实我们当时把 GitHub 上的公开代码做了个快照，放到我们叫“北极代码库”(Arctic Code Vault)的项目里。它基本上就放在芬兰北部，有点像一个种子库(seed vault)。然后我们就想，干脆……
text_es: En realidad habíamos creado una instantánea (snapshot) del código público de GitHub para lo que llamamos la Bóveda de Código Ártico (Arctic Code Vault). O sea, está muy al norte de Finlandia, donde hay una bóveda de semillas (seed vault). Y nos dijimos: “¿sabes qué?”
key_sentence: we had actually created a snapshot of GitHub's public code for what we call the Arctic Code Vault
original_text: We had actually created a snapshot of GitHub's public code for what we call the Arctic Code Vault, right? Essentially, this is up in like way in the Northlands of Finland, there's a seed vault. We were like, you know what? Seed vaults are really there to preserve the diversity of the world's flora in seeds in case of some crazy either natural or manmade disaster. But another really important asset to the world is our code, our open source.

vocabulary.definition: A snapshot is a representation or capture of a system's state at a specific point in time. It allows users to view or restore the system as it was at that moment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech, snapshots are frequently used in version control systems to capture the state of code or data, enabling developers to revert to previous versions or analyze changes over time.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a temporary or momentary capture, and while it is useful for tracking changes, it may not reflect ongoing developments unless regularly updated.

text: The original team that was working on Copilot at GitHub was the team that we call GitHub Next. Essentially their job is to work on second and third horizon projects. What some folks might call moonshots, right?
speaker: Ryan J. Salva
context: Lenny asks whether there was a clear moment when leadership decided to double down on Copilot as a major investment. Ryan explains GitHub's organizational structure for innovation, describing GitHub Next as their R&D team focused on long-term experimental projects. He defines horizon projects as initiatives organized by time and uncertainty rather than calendar dates, with different horizons representing different levels of risk and timeline expectations.
text_ko: GitHub에서 코파일럿(Copilot)을 원래 작업하던 팀이 바로 우리가 깃허브 넥스트(GitHub Next)라고 부르는 팀이에요. 본질적으로 그들의 일은 제2·제3 호라이즌(horizon) 프로젝트를 맡아서 진행하는 거예요. 어떤 사람들은 이런 걸 문샷(moonshots)이라고 부르기도 하죠, 그렇죠?
text_zh: 最早在 GitHub 负责 Copilot 的那支团队，就是我们叫 GitHub Next 的团队。简单来说，他们主要做第二、第三阶段的未来探索项目（second- and third-horizon projects），也就是有些人说的“登月式”项目（moonshots），对吧？
text_es: El equipo original que trabajaba en Copilot en GitHub es el que llamamos GitHub Next. En esencia se ocupan de proyectos a mediano y largo plazo (second and third horizon projects), lo que algunos podrían llamar «moonshots» (moonshots).
key_sentence: GitHub Next works on second and third horizon projects, or moonshots.
original_text: The original team that was working on Copilot at GitHub was the team that we call GitHub Next. Essentially their job is to work on second and third horizon projects. What some folks might call moonshots, right? Things that we never really expect work in the next one or two years, but might three, five years down the line actually turn into something meaningful.

vocabulary.definition: Horizon projects refer to initiatives that are focused on long-term goals and future innovations, typically extending beyond the immediate operational scope of an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, horizon projects are often pursued to explore new markets or technologies that may not yield immediate returns but are essential for future growth and competitiveness.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a forward-thinking approach, emphasizing the importance of balancing current operations with future possibilities.

vocabulary.definition: Moonshots are ambitious, exploratory projects aimed at achieving significant breakthroughs or innovations, often with high risks and uncertain outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup world, moonshots are typically associated with transformative ideas that could disrupt industries or create entirely new markets, often requiring substantial investment and visionary leadership.
vocabulary.nuance: The term conveys a sense of grand ambition and the willingness to take risks for potentially revolutionary results, making it suitable for visionary discussions.

text: Making sure that you've got a good mix of engineers who are comfortable maintaining a service, as well as engineers and researchers who are really thinking about... what is the new thing that we've brought to market.
speaker: Ryan J. Salva
context: Ryan shares lessons learned about transitioning experimental R&D projects to operational products within large companies. He emphasizes the importance of creating hybrid teams that combine researchers who understand the original innovation with engineers who have the skills to scale and maintain production services. This advice comes from GitHub's experience moving Copilot from their experimental Next team to their production engineering teams.
text_ko: 서비스(service)를 안정적으로 운영·유지하는 데 익숙한 엔지니어(engineers)들과, 우리가 시장에 내놓은 것이 진짜로 무엇이 새롭고 의미 있는지 진지하게 고민하는 연구원(researchers)과 엔지니어들이 적절히 섞여 있어야 해요.
text_zh: 要确保团队里有合适的人才搭配：既有对维护服务得心应手的工程师(engineers)，也有真正去思考我们能向市场带来什么新东西的工程师和研究人员(researchers)。
text_es: Asegúrate de contar con una buena mezcla: ingenieros que se sientan cómodos manteniendo el servicio, y otros ingenieros e investigadores que realmente se pregunten qué es lo nuevo que estamos llevando al mercado.
key_sentence: A good mix of engineers can bring that vision to it.
original_text: Making sure that you've got a good mix of engineers who are comfortable maintaining a service, as well as engineers and researchers who are really thinking about, what is the idea that we've created, what is the new thing that we've brought to market, and can bring that vision to it.

vocabulary.definition: Researchers are individuals who systematically investigate and study various subjects to develop new knowledge or insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, researchers play a crucial role in innovation, helping to identify market needs and develop new technologies or products that can be brought to market.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a rigorous, methodical approach to inquiry, and is typically used in contexts where evidence-based findings are valued.

text: As a general rule, as a general principle, I certainly try to make sure that we're always reserving some capacity for bold, audacious experimental research projects. You can think of those really uncertain bets as being five to 10% of the team's capacity.
speaker: Ryan J. Salva
context: Lenny asks Ryan for advice on balancing bold bets versus incremental improvements when managing product portfolios at large companies. Ryan provides specific percentage recommendations for resource allocation: 5-10% on experimental moonshots, 25-30% on maintaining existing products, and about 60% on incremental improvements to in-market products. He notes this framework works for larger teams, while startups typically must go all-in on single big bets.
text_ko: 일반적으로는 저는 대담하고 과감한 실험적 연구 프로젝트(experimental research projects)를 위해 항상 일정한 여력을 남겨두려고 해요. 그런 정말 불확실한 베팅(bets)은 팀 역량의 약 5~10% 정도로 보면 돼요.
text_zh: 通常我会确保团队总留出一点带宽，去做那些大胆、冒险的实验性研究。把这些高度不确定的尝试当作占团队能力大概5%到10%就行。
text_es: Como regla general, procuro que siempre reservemos algo de capacidad para proyectos de investigación experimentales y audaces. Puedes ver esas apuestas muy inciertas como entre el 5% y el 10% de la capacidad del equipo.
key_sentence: We reserve capacity for bold, audacious experimental research projects.
original_text: As a general rule, as a general principle, I certainly try to make sure that we're always reserving some capacity for bold, audacious experimental research projects. You can think of those really uncertain bets as being five to 10% of the team's capacity. About 25, maybe 30% of the team's capacity should generally be on just operations.

vocabulary.definition: Showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks; daring.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'audacious' often describes innovative strategies or projects that challenge the status quo and require significant investment and commitment.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'audacious' conveys a sense of bravery, it can also imply recklessness if not supported by sound reasoning.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or based on untested ideas or methods; involving trial and error.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and tech, 'experimental' refers to projects or initiatives that are in the testing phase, often aimed at innovation or discovering new market opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a focus on innovation and learning, but may also imply uncertainty and potential failure.

vocabulary.definition: The maximum amount that something can contain or produce; the ability to hold or accommodate.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'capacity' often refers to the resources available for production, including human resources, technology, and financial assets, which can impact strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'capacity' generally denotes potential, it can also imply limitations when resources are fully utilized.
